speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are experiencing intense itching and red bumps on your thigh and elsewhere. To help me identify the cause, have these symptoms been present for more than 24 hours, and do they come and go throughout the day?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with intense itching of his right thigh region for the past few days. He also mentions the recent formation of ‘red bumps’ in the same area. The patient has recently attended a business conference in Miami. He has a past medical history of hypertension, diabetes type 2, and hyperlipidemia. The patient’s medication regimen includes enalapril, metformin, and atorvastatin. He denies any history of smoking or drinking.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scabies (likely secondary to a recent outbreak or close contact at the Miami conference). The intense itching, red bumps, recent travel to a high-risk area, and patient demographics strongly suggest this condition. I will confirm this with a skin scraping test if you consent to the examination.
